title: Degreewise component equation for pinned tensor square
statement: Fix schemes $X,X',S,S'$, morphisms $f:X\to S$, $f':X'\to S'$, $g:S'\to S$, $g':X'\to X$, and a cartesian square $sq:\operatorname{IsPullback}(g',f',f,g)$. Assume the derived-category instances of the module-sheaf categories. Let $P,Q$ be arbitrary integer cochain complexes of module sheaves on $X$, $N$ such a complex on $X'$, $H_0=\operatorname{tensorPullback}(g')$ the module pullback functor, $H$ its degreewise extension, and $a:HQ\to N$ a chain map. At $z\in X'$ put $R=\mathcal O_{S,f(g'z)}$, $A=\mathcal O_{X,g'z}$, $B=\mathcal O_{S',f'z}$, $C=\mathcal O_{X',z}$, with the algebra maps induced by the square [def-pc-single-complex-base-change-stalk-condition]. Let $b:A\to A\otimes_R B\to C$ be the resulting composite ring map, $G=\operatorname{extendScalars}(b)$, $F=G$ applied degreewise, $T$ the stalk functor at $g'z$ on $X$, $S$ the stalk functor at $z$ on $X'$ applied degreewise, $U=T(P)$ and $V=T(Q)$. Write $\kappa_L=\operatorname{tensorStalkIso}(f,f',g,g',sq,z,L):F(TL)\cong S(HL)$ for the specified pullback-stalk comparison. Let $e_{L,M}:T\operatorname{Tot}(L\otimes M)\cong TL\otimes TM$ and $e'_{L,M}:S\operatorname{Tot}(L\otimes M)\cong SL\otimes SM$ be the chosen pinned stalk tensor comparisons [lem-pc-tensor-pullback-stalk-square], characterized on each summand by the canonical module tensor-stalk comparison. Define $\sigma=e_{P,Q}^{-1}$, $t=\kappa_Q;S(a)$ and $\rho=(\kappa_P\otimes1_{SN});(e'_{HP,N})^{-1}$. Suppose $\chi:H\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes Q)\cong\operatorname{Tot}(HP\otimes HQ)$ satisfies $H_0(\iota_{P,Q}^{p,q,n});\chi_n=c_{P^p,Q^q};\iota_{HP,HQ}^{p,q,n}$ for every $p+q=n$, where $c$ is the chosen module pullback tensor isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-tensor]. For every integer $n$, the displayed component equality is $(F(\sigma);\kappa_{\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes Q)};S(\chi;(1\otimes a)))_n=(\mu_F^{-1};(1\otimes t);\rho)_n$.

proof.text: Apply HomologicalComplex.mapBifunctor.hom_ext_of_map to scalar extension of the total tensor of U and V. For each p+q=n, the left-summand formula and right-summand formula identify the two precomposed components with the same explicit map δ_G; (κ_P,p tensor κ_Q,q); (1 tensor S(a)_q); ι_{SHP,SN}; e'_{HP,N}.inv_n. Transitivity gives the summand equality and coproduct extensionality gives the component equality.
